title: Visually Exploring Boosted Tree Models
text: Pre-1.0 active development. exists today: five implemented figures complete tested. API exists expected change; list missing, provisional. ggBoostedTrees draws diagnostic figures boosted tree models fit boostmtree, implements Friedman’s gradient descent boosting multivariate tree base learners longitudinal responses, partial support BoostMLR fits (see status table ). boosting counterpart ggRandomForests, follows two-step idiom: extractor pulls tidy data frame fitted model, autoplot() renders . boostmtree fit want know whether converged, package; three five figures also accept BoostMLR fit. full reference — every function changelog — online https://ehrlinger.github.io/ggBoostedTrees/.

title: Visually Exploring Boosted Tree Models
text: ggBoostedTrees requires patched build boostmtree, CRAN release. CRAN’s boostmtree 2.0.0 three defects reach figures: frozen residuals cv.flag = TRUE (exactly flag error path depends ), incorrect na.action handling, malformed dimnames vimp(joint = TRUE). fixes live fork pending upstream merge. requirement enforced rather documented: Imports floor boostmtree (>= 2.0.1), CRAN’s 2.0.0 satisfy . install defective backend fails resolve instead silently producing wrong figures. Remotes: field points fork, correct boostmtree installed . install backend :

title: Visually Exploring Boosted Tree Models
text: Fit model cv.flag = TRUE, ask whether converged: cv.flag = TRUE optional error path. boostmtree records err.rate m.opt cross-validation ran, default fit error path draw gg_boost_error() say . Every figure available data well plot, tidy frame point rather implementation detail: variance smoothing parameter paths diagnose whether variance structure settled boosting stopped. always faceted free y scale, rho, phi lambda span three orders magnitude: trajectory plot one longitudinal boosting exists — whether model tracks individual subjects, just population mean:
code: library(ggBoostedTrees)  set.seed(7) sim <- boostmtree::simLong(n = 25, n.time = 4, model = 1)$data.list fit <- boostmtree::boostmtree(   x = sim$features, tm = sim$time, id = sim$id, y = sim$y,   M = 50, cv.flag = TRUE, verbose = FALSE,   control = boostmtree::boostmtree.control(seed = 7) )  # The error path, with the cross-validated optimal iteration marked. autoplot(fit) gg_dta <- gg_boost_error(fit) head(gg_dta, 3) #>   iteration     value response optimal #> 1         1 1.0118738        y   FALSE #> 2         2 1.0008788        y   FALSE #> 3         3 0.9912097        y   FALSE  # Returns a bare ggplot, so it composes with any theme or scale. autoplot(gg_dta) + ggplot2::theme_bw() autoplot(gg_boost_path(fit)) autoplot(gg_boost_trajectory(fit))

Neither source computes confidence interval, none reported . boostmtree accepts factor covariates. , partial.plot() marginal.plot() return character (, marginal.plot()$data, factor) x column one row per level rather numeric grid. gg_boost_effect detects maps level integer position x, carrying level x_label; continuous covariate keeps numeric value x leaves x_label NA. grid resolved per variable every time point shares level ordering. gg_boost_effect currently single-response . boostmtree nests $curves / $smooth [[response]][[variable]] flattens outer level fit single response; multi-response object rejected informative error rather mishandled. also gg_boost_effect one class five without response column.

title: Boosting parameter path data object — gg_boost_path
text: boostmtree re-estimates three quantities every boosting iteration: rho, within-subject correlation; phi, variance component; lambda, P-spline smoothing parameter time-covariate interaction. paths diagnose whether variance structure settled still drifting boosting stops. Unlike error path, recorded every fit require cv.flag = TRUE. parameter absent fit dropped silently; error none requested parameters present. figure also accepts BoostMLR fit, records Rho Phi M--response matrices – method's default parameters c("rho", "phi") rather three. BoostMLR comparable lambda: Lambda_List holds per-iteration basis coefficients rather scalar smoothing parameter per response, different quantity, requesting "lambda" BoostMLR fit refused reason instead silently dropped.

title: Subject trajectory data object — gg_boost_trajectory
text: figure longitudinal boosting exists : whether model tracks individual subjects time, rather fitting population mean. boostmtree stores time, mu y.org parallel lists per-subject vectors, order observations supplied rather time order. Rows sorted time within subject, assembled frame response-major (subjects one response, next), line drawn one subject's rows follows trajectory instead zigzagging. Subject identifiers come fit's id.unique, positional index. observed NA throughout fit carries observed response, happens prediction new data. figure accepts either boostmtree BoostMLR fit. BoostMLR stores mu y flat observation--response matrices, tm id parallel flat vectors, rather boostmtree's nested per-subject lists – entirely different layout information. Response labels come y_Names, since mu carries column names. BoostMLR natively multi-response, fit typically yields several response blocks even "single" model.

title: ggBoostedTrees 0.0.6
text: BoostMLR fits now accepted gg_boost_trajectory(), gg_boost_error() gg_boost_path(). Adding backend required extractor methods ; renderer changed, tidy intermediate exists guarantee. BoostMLR selects optimal boosting iteration, gg_boost_error() flags none backend rather deriving one. BoostMLR’s Lambda_List holds per-iteration basis coefficients rather scalar smoothing parameter, gg_boost_path() offers rho phi backend says lambda requested. gg_boost_vimp() gg_boost_effect() remain boostmtree . gg_boost_error() refuses use.rmse BoostMLR fit whether passed name position. generic declares second formal, positional form valid syntax, previously fell returned standardized values caller asked scale. autoplot.gg_boost_trajectory() accepts repeated subject identifier subset rather failing internal factor level [2] duplicated. caller’s ordering still determines factor levels. gg_boost_path()’s boostmtree method validates parameters way BoostMLR sibling gg_boost_vimp()’s components argument : empty vector rejected duplicates de-duplicated rather reaching opaque factor() error.
